To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) job performance and job satisfaction are positively correlated, (ii) job performance is not only affected by economic incentives, (iii) job performance is positively affected by intrinsic motivations, and (iv) self-esteem helps explain job performance and job satisfactions.
(i) job satisfaction is a function of intrinsic motivation and self-esteem, and (ii) job performance is a function of job satisfaction, intrinsic motivation, and self-esteem.
job satisfaction and job effort are both positively correlated with the intrinsic motivation to do the job and with self-esteem.

the economic approach to job performance and satisfaction can be enriched by the insights provided by organisational psychology and by the empirical evidence from the literature on job satisfaction.
